page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.12xlarge is a storage-optimized server powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8559C processors built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 48 virtual CPUs, corresponding to 24 physical cores with hyper-threading, operating at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz and supported by a 320 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The server includes a massive local storage array of 30,000 GB on NVMe SSDs and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps under the Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate strong capabilities across memory and processing tasks. The server achieves top-tier performance in Geekbench single-core metrics and image processing, alongside strong results in multi-core processing, software compilation, and ray tracing. Memory bandwidth tests show strong performance for both cached small-block reads and uncached large-block read and write operations. Database operations, including Redis SET execution, and static web serving throughput also rank in the top 25% tier. For machine learning workloads, the CPU's Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instruction sets support strong text generation and prompt processing speeds for small to medium LLM models, though performance drops to average for larger 70B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the i7ie.12xlarge offers high resource density by bundling massive local NVMe SSD capacity with a high-performance DDR5 memory array. This hardware profile eliminates the need for external network-attached storage for data-intensive operations, optimizing resource utilization. The server is highly suited for large-scale database deployments, high-throughput Redis caching layers, data-intensive web serving, and memory-heavy analytical workloads that require rapid local storage access.
